leads.summary: Open #13286's native brightness wrapper cannot accept this PR's --force wake argument
leads.location: bin/omarchy-system-wake:8; bin/omarchy-brightness-display:17-20; open PR #13286 bin/omarchy-brightness-display wrapper
leads.consequence: The two branches are not stacked. A three-way merge has a real conflict in bin/omarchy-brightness-display; if it is resolved in favor of #13286's `exec omarchy-media brightness display "$@"` without adding --force to the native package, every omarchy-system-wake calls the native binary with --force on. At omarchy-media v0.1.1 src/main.rs:75-102 --force is treated as the brightness step and on is never read; lines 139-160 are not reached, so there is no DPMS enable, even for a dark monitor. An internal panel goes through invalid-step handling at lines 193-197 and the native command exits with an error, while wake continues with keyboard and clamshell commands (system-wake:9-10). The merged test file retains the new --force dispatch assertion and will fail with the native wrapper. Resolve the conflict by porting and testing --force in omarchy-media before replacing this script (or retain this script's implementation); #13286 is separately not yet installable as noted in its own description.
leads.triage: confirmed factual by coordinator (omarchy-media v0.1.1 src/main.rs brightness_display) and Opus self-check; also mentioned in Opus Q4; published in Details

leads.summary: The changed comment's modeset-flash premise is already prevented by Hyprland's same-state early return
leads.consequence: For Hyprland's reported dpmsStatus=true, its actual setDPMS(true) returns before changing or committing output state. Therefore the existing plain-on guard is not required to prevent an extra modeset from a redundant enable on the shipped compositor. The guard instead creates a potential false negative when compositor state is stale (as this PR's description itself says), though --force still only sends a command, not a hardware recovery. This is an inaccurate causal explanation in the changed comment; do not present it as evidence that forced enable repairs NVIDIA s2idle, or that a redundant enable flashes every panel. The guard itself predates this PR.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (H3); corroboration; not published separately (comment wording note covers the comment)

leads.summary: The new ordinary-on skip test passes even if ordinary wake never enables a dark monitor
leads.consequence: The new stub emits only dpmsStatus:true. A disposable mutant adding `exit 0` inside the !force branch before the status query passed the complete brightness-display test including the --force assertion; on a dpmsStatus:false fixture, ordinary `on` exits 0 with no hyprctl call. Thus a plausible regression that breaks normal wake will pass. Add a dark enabled-panel fixture and assert that ordinary on dispatches enable.
leads.triage: confirmed factual (test file only mocks lit monitor) and reproduced independently by Opus review4; published as optional test improvement with Opus's actual output

leads.summary: Static system-wake test counts a commented-out force call as an executed call
leads.consequence: After commenting out `omarchy-brightness-display --force on` in a disposable copy of bin/omarchy-system-wake, the new grep still matches the comment and the complete monitor-recovery suite passes; invoking that wake with stubs records only keyboard restore and clamshell, not display wake. Add a command-spy execution test to assert the actual --force on argv.

limits: No actual NVIDIA suspend/resume device or desktop allocated, so whether this user's panel can be restored by a disable/enable cycle remains untested and is not inferred from stubs. Hyprland source settles only compositor behavior at matched versions.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** `Closes #13251` would close the issue although the forced enable commits nothing in the reported state.

Status at `fccec59` since the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13259#issuecomment-5854659032):
- Failing `--force on` test: resolved.
- Hyprland drops the enable while `dpmsStatus` is true: still present (PR description now says so).
- Wake-path wording: description fixed; the code comment and a test label still describe the old split.

### `Closes #13251` closes the issue without a confirmed fix

`quattro` is the default branch, so merging closes #13251. Per Hyprland source (not reproduced), `CMonitor::setDPMS` returns early when the status is already on (v0.55.0 to `main`), so it commits nothing in that state. **Impact:** the issue could close before any test on the affected laptop.

**Suggested change:** Use `Refs #13251` until the reporter confirms a fix.

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (isolated sandbox, mocked `hyprctl`):
- `brightness-display-test.sh` passes at `fccec59`, fails with the base script on the `--force` case, and fails for a deleted guard and for a `--force` flag that is parsed but ignored.
- `monitor-recovery-test.sh` passes at `fccec59` and fails with the base script.
- Both pass on the current `quattro` tip with the PR applied. The lock and idle changes on `quattro` since the merge-base do not change when `omarchy-system-wake` runs.

**Comment wording:** `bin/omarchy-brightness-display` says the guard avoids a flash "(e.g. lock-screen keystroke wake)", and the new test label in `monitor-recovery-test.sh` says "after resume". Lock-screen input runs `omarchy-system-wake`, which now forces, so both describe the old split. For example: "Plain `on` skips the enable when every enabled monitor already reports lit. `omarchy-system-wake` (lock-screen input, auth, cancelled idle) passes `--force`."

**Related PRs:**
- #12210 is unchanged and merges cleanly with this PR. Its extra enable after `omarchy-system-wake` would duplicate the forced one.
- Draft #13286 replaces this script's body with `exec omarchy-media brightness display "$@"`. The `omarchy-media` v0.1.1 parser takes `--force` as the brightness step, so after that change `omarchy-system-wake` would no longer send the enable. Whichever lands second needs to carry `--force` over.
</details>

<details><summary>Optional notes</summary>

- **Optional test improvement:** the brightness test's DPMS cases only mock a lit monitor. A mutant that makes plain `on` exit before the status check (so a dark panel never gets the enable) still passes the whole file. A dark-panel case catches it:

  ```bash
  cat >"$mock_bin/hyprctl" <<'SH'
  #!/bin/bash
  printf 'hyprctl %s\n' "$*" >>"$CALL_LOG"
  if [[ $* == 'monitors -j' ]]; then
    printf '%s\n' '[{"name":"eDP-1","disabled":false,"dpmsStatus":false}]'
  fi
  SH
  chmod +x "$mock_bin/hyprctl"
  : >"$call_log"
  run_brightness --no-osd on
  if ! grep -F 'dispatch hl.dsp.dpms({ action = "enable" })' "$call_log" >/dev/null; then
    fail "on dispatches DPMS enable when an enabled panel reports dark"
  fi
  pass "on dispatches DPMS enable when an enabled panel reports dark"
  ```

  Actual output (sandbox, mocked `hyprctl`), with the mutant adding `exit 0` inside the plain-`on` branch before the status check:

  Mutant, current file, exit 0:
  ```text
  ok - named Apple display is detected independently of focus
  ok - on skips DPMS enable when every panel already reports lit
  ok - --force on dispatches DPMS enable despite stale dpmsStatus
  ```

  Mutant, with the case added, exit 1:
  ```text
  ok - named Apple display is detected independently of focus
  ok - on skips DPMS enable when every panel already reports lit
  ok - --force on dispatches DPMS enable despite stale dpmsStatus
  not ok - on dispatches DPMS enable when an enabled panel reports dark
  ```

  `fccec59` with the case added passes (exit 0).

- **Optional test improvement:** the two new cases call the script directly, not through `run_brightness`, so they do not get the test's private `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`. With the base script, the `--force on` case falls through to the brightness path, leaves a lock file in the caller's runtime directory and calls the OSD. `run_brightness --no-osd on` and `run_brightness --no-osd --force on` give the same pass/fail results without those side effects (checked in the sandbox).
</details>
